I've installed agy (1.2.11) in this container. It isn't signed in yet, so that's the one step left before a run can have AGY as the manager.

**What you need to do:** open this URL, sign in with Google, and copy the code it shows:

https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth?access_type=offline&client_id=1071006060591-tmhssin2h21lcre235vtolojh4g403ep.apps.googleusercontent.com&code_challenge=9Uy497afH1zj302svYJ8Aq-swQg593ckPf451Ar8nRQ&code_challenge_method=S256&prompt=consent&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fantigravity.google%2Foauth-callback&response_type=code&scope=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fcloud-platform+https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fuserinfo.email+https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fuserinfo.profile+https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fcclog+https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fexperimentsandconfigs+https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Faicode+openid&state=uOQxJxGBXMqm-DR_jxwVIQ

Paste the code here. I'll run `agy-login.sh --code '<code>'`, then check with `agy-doctor.sh --probe`. The login keeps waiting in the background, so the URL stays valid until this session resets.

The health check already passes on everything except sign-in: agy is on PATH, the keyring works, the dev-loop skill is installed for Antigravity, and 22 permission grants are written.

**The setup script was broken, and I fixed it.** It failed twice with "cannot execute binary file" before the third try worked. The cause is antigravity.google's CDN: one cache node sends the installer gzip-compressed even though the download never asked for compression. It hit 2 of the 6 downloads I tested, and the script saved those compressed bytes as-is.
- **Fix:** a new helper, `scripts/env/fetch-installer.sh`, downloads with curl's `--compressed` flag, which unpacks the response, and refuses anything that isn't a shell script. `setup-antigravity.sh` now uses it, and `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` has the same fix inline.
- **Test:** `tests/test_agy_installer_fetch.py` runs a local server that always compresses the response. The helper recovers the script exactly. It correctly rejects the compressed bytes when the flag is removed, and rejects an HTML page. Undoing either part of the fix makes the test fail.
- **Real site:** 6 of 6 downloads through the helper came back identical, and the full repo check (`validate.sh`) passes.
- **Not checked:** I didn't rebuild the devcontainer image.

It's up as PR #20, ready for review: https://github.com/mios-dev/-dev-loop/pull/20. I'm watching it for CI results and review comments, with a check-in scheduled in an hour. Once agy is signed in, tell me what the run should work on; the three backlog tasks I offered earlier (T-1070, the replay tests, T-1073) are still options.
